title.english: Umayma bint Khalaf ibn As'ad ibn Amir ibn Subay' al-Khuza'iyya[3]

segments.arabic:
١٠٨٥١- أميمة بنت خلف «٣»
بن أسعد بن عامر بن سبيع الخزاعية، عمة طلحة الطلحات الجواد المشهور.
كانت زوج خالد بن سعيد بن العاص، فأسلمت قديما وهاجرت معه إلى الحبشة.
ويقال: اسمها أمينة «٤»، بالنون بدل الميم، ويقال همينة بالهاء بدل الألف، فولدت له أم خالد بنت خالد فسماها آمنة، واشتهرت بكنيتها.
segments.english:
10851 — Umayma bint Khalaf ibn As'ad ibn Amir ibn Subay' al-Khuza'iyya[3]

She was the paternal aunt of Talha al-Talahat, the renowned generous man.

She was the wife of Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-As. She embraced Islam at an early date and emigrated with him to Abyssinia.

Her name is also said to have been Amina,[4] with a nun in place of the second mim; and it is also said to have been Humayna, with a ha in place of the alif. She bore him Umm Khalid bint Khalid, whom he named Amina, and she became known by her kunya.

names.arabic: أميمة بنت خلف بن أسعد بن عامر بن سبيع الخزاعية
names.english: Umayma bint Khalaf ibn As'ad ibn Amir ibn Subay' al-Khuza'iyya
Amina bint Khalaf ibn As'ad ibn Amir ibn Subay' al-Khuza'iyya
Humayna bint Khalaf ibn As'ad ibn Amir ibn Subay' al-Khuza'iyya

unresolved.explanation: The canonical Arabic and the supplied Urdu and Usd al-Ghaba witnesses establish the consonants but do not decisively establish the vowels. Humayna has therefore been retained provisionally; al-Isti'ab supplies a different consonantal variant, هميمة, rather than resolving the vocalization.
